system_message:
Bạn là WRITER — thực thi đúng **chapter prompt** được cung cấp.

## QUY TẮC
1. Đọc toàn bộ chapter prompt (bible, đã xảy ra, kỹ thuật, spice, việc cần làm).
2. Đọc story_state — KHÔNG mâu thuẫn facts_established, timeline, character_status.
3. Viết đúng spice level trong prompt. Đúng cliffhanger.
4. **1600-1900 words (min 1250). Dưới 1250 = thất bại** — ưu tiên đối thoại + nội tâm DT để đủ dài. Không tóm tắt; viết full scene đến đủ độ dài.
5. ENGLISH ONLY — no Vietnamese diacritics, no CJK/Hangul characters.
6. Không lặp banned_phrases từ state.
7. Output **chỉ prose chương** — không chain-of-thought, không planning, không meta.
8. **KHÔNG markdown trong prose** — cấm `**bold**`, `*italic*`, backtick, `## heading`, `**Cliffhanger:**`. Chỉ plain text; dialogue dùng dấu ngoặc kép `"..."`. Dòng đầu duy nhất được `# Chapter N: Title` (hoặc `# Chương N: Tiêu đề`).

## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS (khi có block trong prompt)
Block **## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS** (hoặc RÀNG BUỘC NARRATIVE) có authority cao hơn suy diễn tự do:
- **Clues to PLANT:** phải gieo trong chương — subtle, không giải thích payoff sớm.
- **Clues to PAY OFF:** chỉ payoff clue đã plant trước đó; đúng nghĩa `true_meaning`.
- **Reveals:** chỉ hé đúng reveal của chương này; không spoil reveal chương sau.
- **MUST NOT know:** nhân vật không được biết/nói/nghĩ những fact bị cấm — kể cả nội tâm.
- Không mâu thuẫn block này dù `must_happen` plan có vẻ rộng hơn.

Ngôn ngữ đích: **English**.

Output: **chỉ nội dung chương** (`# Chương N: Tiêu đề` hoặc `# Chapter N: Title`), không meta, không JSON, không checklist.

# Chapter 3: The First Examination

The tunnel smelled of damp concrete. Iris Kane started at the mouth, counting liner segments. Theo Vance followed three paces behind.

The lighting was low—emergency LEDs spaced every thirty meters—casting uneven pools that left the curves of the tunnel in half-shadow. The Kessler Line had been sealed since the collapse, and the air had settled into a stale density that tasted of rust and sealant.

Iris ran her thumb along the first segment. The surface was smooth. Intact. The official report listed a seismic microfracture pattern initiating at segment forty-two. She had read the telemetry logs. Nothing in the dispatch data mentioned unusual vibration before the collapse.

The tunnel curved gently to the left. Her footsteps echoed against the concrete, a flat rhythm in the dead air. Theo's steps were irregular, stopping and starting. He checked his phone twice before they reached the first bend.

"It doesn't look like a seismic event," she said.

"It wouldn't, visually."

"What would it look like?"

"Crack patterns radiating from a focal point. Spalling around bolt housings."

"I know what it looks like," Iris said. "I am asking if you have seen it."

A pause. "No."

"But you signed off on the inspection scope."

"The scope was set by the terms of the mandate."

"Which you wrote."

"Which I coordinated."

She stopped walking and turned. The emergency light caught half his face. The other half stayed in shadow.

"Every effort has been made to confine the investigation," she said.

"Who made the effort?"

"The mandate was designed before I was appointed."

"That is not what I asked."

"It is the only answer I have."

"You are deflecting."

"I am surviving."

She held his gaze for a moment, then resumed counting. Thirty-eight. Thirty-nine. Forty. Forty-one.

Forty-two.

The segment was darker than the others. The concrete had a slight patina, but the certification plate was bright, the letters crisp. She stopped in front of it.

"Tell me about Marek."

"I already sent you his file."

"Files are curated. I want your impression."

Theo ran a hand through his hair. A clean gesture, practiced. "Dov was a site inspector. He was thorough. Company loyal. Avoided conflict."

"Thorough and conflict-avoidant are adjacent but not the same."

"They can live in the same person."

"Was he capable of forging a certification?"

Theo's steps slowed. "I don't know."

"You knew him."

"I knew him well enough to know he followed orders."

"Whose orders?"

"His supervisors'. The chain of command."

"That is not an answer."

"It is the only one I have."

The certification plate was fixed to the wall at eye level. Dov Marek's name. A date stamp. A signature. She ran her nail along the edge of the plate. It was rigid. Official-looking.

She knelt and examined the concrete around the base.

The dust was a different shade. A lighter grey, almost white. The rest of the liner had aged into a uniform charcoal. She scraped a thin layer with her finger. It came free easily, finer than the rest of the liner. Ground recently.

"The certification says this segment was installed and stamped before the tunnel went live."

"Yes."

"The concrete under this plate has been ground within the last year."

Theo said nothing.

She touched the stamp. The paint was thick, semi-gloss. It transferred to her glove without resistance, a clean half-circle on the white fabric.

"The paint is not old enough to match the installation date," she said. "The protocol requires the stamp to be applied before the liner leaves the casting yard, while the concrete is still curing. This was applied here, in the tunnel, to a surface that had already been ground smooth."

"That is an observation," Theo said carefully.

"It is an invitation to test. I want a core sample from this exact point."

Theo's phone buzzed.

He did not answer it.

"Did you know?"

"Know what?"

"That the certification was post-dated."

"I knew Marek was dead."

Iris stood. Her knee was damp from the concrete. "When did he die?"

"Nine months ago. Before the collapse."

"His signature is on a stamp applied within the last six months."

Theo's phone buzzed again. He pulled it from his pocket, glanced at the screen, and put it back without a word.

"Are you going to answer that?"

"No."

"Who is it?"

"I don't know."

"You looked."

"The screen was blank."

"You are lying."

Theo met her eyes. His face was unreadable in the dim light. "I am trying to keep you on the evidence."

"Then stay on it. The anomaly is recorded. Marek's signature is on a certification that was applied after the concrete was re-ground. The timeline is broken. The official theory cannot hold."

"The anomaly is recorded," she repeated. "I want a core sample from this exact point."

"The authorization will take time."

"I am authorizing it. The inquiry has independent access to the physical evidence. That was the condition of my appointment."

"The condition was access," Theo said. "Not destruction."

"A core sample is not destruction. It is analysis."

He looked at the plate. His jaw tightened. "It will generate a paper trail."

"Good. I want one."

"They will ask why."

"Tell them I found something that does not fit."

"What did you find?"

She knelt again. The paint was still wet on her glove. She touched the certification stamp a second time, pressing harder. The lettering blurred under her thumb.

"The paint transfer and the dust difference are not conclusive on their own," she said. "Concrete can age unevenly in a sealed tunnel. But the protocol requirement is clear. The anomaly contradicts the official record. A core sample will determine when the surface was last mechanically ground. Until then, the certification is suspect."

"The certification is the record."

"The record is a piece of stamped concrete. And this piece tells a different story than the one in your binder."

Theo's phone buzzed a third time.

He did not touch it.

Iris stood and faced him. "I came here to examine the physical evidence. I have done that. I have identified an inconsistency that needs to be resolved before I can sign my name to any conclusion. The inspection does not end here. It begins with the sample."

"The lab will need a request form."

"Then provide one."

"The form requires a reason."

"The reason is that the certification on segment forty-two was not applied at the time of installation. The concrete has been re-ground. The paint is fresh. The timeline is broken. I want a core sample from this exact point to establish the sequence."

She held his gaze. He did not look away.

"Iris."

"I am not asking for permission, Theo. I am telling you what I am doing."

His phone buzzed a fourth time. The sound was sharp against the silence of the tunnel.

"Aren't you going to answer it?"

"No."

"It could be important."

"It is not."

"How do you know?"

"Because I know who it is."

"Then who?"

He looked at the screen. The light cast a brief glow across his face.

"I cannot tell you."

"You can. You are choosing not to."

"I am choosing to survive."

"Then survive silently. I am ordering the core sample. You can tell whoever is calling that the evidence was compromised before they had a chance to clean it."

Theo's hand tightened around the phone. His knuckles went white.

"You do not know what you are stepping into."

"I am stepping into a tunnel where a piece of concrete was ground and stamped with a dead man's signature. I know exactly what I am stepping into. I just don't know how deep it goes."

"The danger is not in the depth."

"Then where is it?"

"In the people who built the tunnel at every level."

"Iris knelt and touched the liner certification. The paint came off on her glove. 'This certification wasn't applied at installation,' she said. 'The concrete underneath has been re-ground within the operating lifespan of the tunnel. The anomaly is recorded. I want a core sample from this exact point to establish the timeline.'

Theo Vance said nothing. His phone buzzed. He didn't answer it."
